facts.claim: Sacra estimates Infleqtion generated $31.1M of 2025 revenue and reports H1 2026 revenue of $23.4M, up 74% year over year, with Q2 revenue of $13.5M after the company's revenue-recognition update.
Sacra reports approximately 83% of H1 2026 revenue came from government customers and about 74% from the U.S. government, indicating material customer/funding concentration despite strong growth.

Sacra reports H1 2026 service mix at 71% of revenue and describes current gross margins as constrained by engineering-heavy government program work, making mix shift and contract execution important to the commercialization thesis.

risks.risk: Government-customer concentration makes revenue durability sensitive to funding priorities, renewals and follow-on awards.
Strong top-line growth does not by itself establish scalable product economics while the mix remains service- and engineering-heavy.

contradictions.contradiction: Rapid 2026 revenue growth coexists with high government concentration and low-margin engineering-heavy work; commercialization progress is real but revenue quality and scalability remain underwriting questions.

unknowns.unknown: Alpha still must determine source-addressed numeric factor values, normalized margin/cash-burn treatment and final data-confidence evidence under Methodology 1.0.
